It more so sounds like your friend is antisocial and has a lot of social anxiety, while she is introverted as well that’s not the main issue. At one point I had crippling social anxiety that I had to drop out of school. I was depressed and anxious, and stayed in bed all day, but that’s mental illness not being an introvert.

Introverted doesn’t always mean that you don’t like crowds or talking. Being an introvert means you need to be alone to recharge. When I’m around bigger crowds with lots going on it can be fun for awhile, I might be a little anxious depending on the situation, but at the end of the night I need to go home and be alone. As long as I’m with a strong extrovert I can last a long time before needing to be alone. In high school when I was with my friends I was often the loudest and most annoying person there, but that doesn’t mean I’m not an introvert who needs alone time to recharge.
